2026-07-17-dive-radio-bumpy-takeoff|drop.summary: The hosts own up to first-show jank — a botched AI intro video, a rushed brand refresh — and welcome viewers to the first, admittedly bumpy, Dive Radio livestream.
Industry-news riffing: the hosts react to designer moves — big names leaving for Cursor — and debate whether running design at a fast-scaling company is a job anyone should want.
Wind-down talk at the very end: the hosts trade late-night work-habit confessions — chasing an idea until early morning — and joke that none of it should be taken as advice.

2026-07-23-dive-radio-data-vs-intuition-.summary: A portfolio showcase: one host screen-shares designer Sid's playful, personal portfolio and tells how he found him through the talent network, while the audience vote gets set up.
Recorded community nominations play back to back: a nominee signs off by nominating another designer, and the hosts riff on the videos' one-liners and self-edited craft between clips.
The hosts read through a community write-up on what design engineering actually is, recommend it on screen, then turn it into a debate about where designers should position themselves.

2026-07-30-dive-radio-mixed-media-workfl.summary: The nomination chain continues — a recorded video hands the torch to an engineer at Resend — and the hosts talk about how the pay-it-forward format started and why it is becoming their favorite segment.

A talk stretch on AI demo overload: the hosts argue the viral demos are really experiments in chaining tools together — mixed-media workflows — not finished products, and that people judge them wrong.
A live gameplay demo, music and all: one host plays an AI-built game on screen — running out of missiles, fumbling a landing — while framing it as a playable experiment, not a market-ready game.
The maker explains an AI catching its own broken model — the mesh was unworkable vector soup — and re-meshing it, then walks through the wiki-fed critic agent they use to gate what counts as good.

2026-08-06-dive-radio-backyard-designers.summary: A recorded nomination praising a jaw-dropping WebGL demo wraps up, and the hosts riff on the double nomination and how comforting it is to hear a master admit he didn't know how he pulled it off.

The backyard-project team gets candid about the launch: feedback lists and voice notes pouring in unprompted, the game becoming something they never set out to make, and asking designers what would help.

One of the makers screen-shares a story deck generated by voice with an AI design tool reading the game's own codebase — built in the final hours before the show — and tests whether its images stay consistent.

2026-08-13-dive-radio-goodbye-blank-canv.summary: A recorded nomination from designer James McDonald plays, and one host detours into a family story about everyone imitating James's accent for a week while editing his podcast episode.
The hosts scroll a community pile-on: replies roasting an AI-generated design post, delete-this jokes included, while they debate how seriously to take the backlash.

Show-and-tell of a community-made card game site: the hosts admire its productized admin flow — drag a card and it deploys — until the site's autoplaying music derails the segment and they close the tab.
A guest walks through how their prototyping workflow changed — from making messes on top of the production codebase to isolated quick mockups — and shares a screen of the new setup.

Hosts chat about tinkering with shaders, then one nominates Rive animator Bartek, showing his flaming sentiment slider, before urging listeners to vote for designer of the week.
Hosts play a teaser clip of a guest, John, on giving agents little characters, recount debates inside Cursor over what became Grokbot, and turn to mascots like Duolingo and Claude.
Host live-tinkers with open source mascot builders, tweaking eyes and movement, showing cute animal characters, then reveals a detailed mixed media mascot of his co-host in sneakers.
Host demos a homemade SVG story animator named for his daughter, guiding a character uphill with a stamina bar, while the co-host talks about making stories with his own kid.
Hosts debate going all in on one AI tool ecosystem, react to Microsoft's flatter Copilot logo, and compare agentic coding interfaces from Cursor, Hermes, and Grokbot.
A host screen-shares open source mascot tools, tweaking blob eyes and motion for a dive character, plugs sponsor Lovable, and riffs on cute animal logos and children's books.
Hosts chat about making stories with their kids, plug the designer of the week vote, then bring caller DJ on air and troubleshoot his missing audio while asking the chat to confirm sound.

Hosts react to a flatter Copilot logo redesign and rebrand workload, then compare agentic coding tools and UIs, recalling an interview where a Cursor hire predicted the shift to chat-style task management.

Host walks through tech mascots like Mico, Nosey, Kit and a Vercel triangle character, then plays a clip of hardware creator Daniel Kuntz advising teams to hire real character animators over coding animations.

Hosts discuss mascots as attachment strategy, read a viewer comment on logos losing meaning, plug sponsor Lovable, then demo open-source blob character tools live, tweaking eyes, rotation and expressions.
Hosts tour brand mascots like Duo, Mico, Nosey, and Kit, praise a playful onboarding, then play a clip of Daniel Kuntz describing the tools built for his character.
A host live-demos open-source blob and mascot tools, resizing eyes and rotation on the show character, mentions sponsor Lovable, and shows expressiveness prototypes.
Hosts tease upcoming show notes, debate a group declaring war on UI animations, discuss a scroll-jacking crab experiment, then try again to connect caller DJ.
Hosts wrap up the show, praising point-and-click design tools, thanking community submissions, plugging the weekly livestream, teasing next week's prototypes, and naming a winner.

2026-08-13-dive-radio-goodbye-blank-canv.summary: Hosts weigh Figma and Lovable valuations as prototyping signals, then Nad's recorded message announces a funding round and asks why so few designers found startups.
Hosts discuss designers building lookalike tools and leaning into distribution, then turn to Benji's Grockbot release, its mascot animation, and one host's preferred OpenClaw setup.

2026-08-28-dive-radio-steal-these-ai-des.summary: Hosts open the show joking about early beta access to a Figma feature and working from home, then set up the main topic: interface patterns in agentic AI design tools.
A host nominates designer Alex for designer of the week, praising his work on Honk and other apps, while the other host screen-shares a live voting page with competing progress bars.
Hosts tour a new design community site by Charles, signing up live on stream, praising its design, debating how to label experiments versus work, and offering viewers an invite.
A host walks through AI patterns: progressive disclosure in chatbots, Paper's corner working animation, and prompting an agent inside Framer to add a pulse to a hero pill.
